title: Console Ops Mode: scope-trim for compact dashboard, tracing-lite, and cost-summary
creator: Marco Li
description: Goal: reduce launch risk and implementation time by trimming the Redwood Console MVP surface to a compact, high-value 'Ops Mode' focused on 1) top-level route and model cost summary, 2) a lightweight trace viewer with sampling and breadcrumb context, and 3) compact dashboard cards that surface SLO, p50/p95 latency, and per-route token counts. This ticket captures the scope decisions, acceptance criteria, and follow-up backlog items for features we explicitly defer or cut to meet the 2025.12 release date.
decisions: Keep: single-tier compact dashboard with 3 card types (Cost Summary, Latency Vitals, Route Throughput). Defer rich drilldowns and custom card assembly to post-MVP.
Cut: interactive flamegraphs, full trace waterfall visualization, and ad-hoc trace search across arbitrary time windows — replaced by sampled trace list + lightweight span timeline.
Cut: per-token heatmap and token-level cost explorer — replaced by aggregated route-level token counts and daily delta chart.
Keep: trace sampling policy UI (preset values only) but remove per-route custom sampling rules for MVP to reduce surface area.
Rollout: soft-launch behind feature flag 'ops-mode-compact' and enable for internal accounts + pilot customers before GA.
Metrics: implement a single aggregated cost annotation pipeline for top routes; defer per-customer cost attribution until dedicated capacity integration is stable.
UX: provide help-to-fallback text for deferred features linking to 'how to reproduce' docs and roadmap entry.
Performance: batch initial dashboard queries and use a 5s polling cadence to maintain p95 load < 300ms for dashboard requests under typical usage.
Acceptance gating: shipping requires design sign-off on compact cards and an SLO for dashboard rendering times (see acceptance_criteria).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: Deploy three compact cards (Cost Summary, Latency Vitals, Route Throughput) with documented API responses and snapshot tests for default viewport.
Dashboard rendering: p95 server render latency for card payloads <= 300ms under 250 concurrent users in staging (measured using console-load-run-2025-11).
Cost Summary: shows 24h and 7d aggregated cost deltas per route and total cost; numbers reconcile within 5% of billing pipeline sample for top-10 routes.
Tracing-lite: users can view sampled traces for a route, open a trace to see span list with timestamps, and see breadcrumb context. Opening a sampled trace should load within 600ms p95.
Trace sampling UI: preset sampling toggles (0.1%, 1%, 5%) available in the trace settings; changes apply within 10 minutes and are visible in sampled trace output.
Graceful degradation: when the cost pipeline is delayed, dashboard cards show last-valid snapshot with a timestamp and a link to troubleshooting docs.
Feature flag: 'ops-mode-compact' must exist and gate the new UI; telemetry must record flag-enabled sessions for rollout analysis.
E2E: automated smoke tests validate core flows (open dashboard, open trace, change sampling preset) in CI; tests added to console-e2e-suite with pass rate >= 95%.
Documentation: a short PRD update, a Designer-approved Figma mock, and a 'deferred-features' README mapping cut items to follow-up tickets must be attached to the ticket before merge.
Security/compliance: no additional PII or unencrypted logs are introduced by the sampling UI; security sign-off recorded if any changes to log retention or KMS paths are required.

risks: Metrics reconciliation drift: aggregated cost may differ from billing pipeline for small routes — risk mitigated by explicit 5% acceptance tolerance and post-launch audit runbook.
Trace sampling latency: if sampler backpressure occurs, sampled traces may be delayed beyond SLAs — mitigation: backpressure circuit and clear UX message.
User confusion: cutting deep-dive features could frustrate power users; mitigation: clear doc and in-product messaging with a route to request full tracing access.
Rollout complexity: feature flag gating and telemetry are necessary to monitor crash rates; ensure ENG instrumentation is in place before pilot.
Design debt: compact cards may require rework for accessibility and localization; schedule follow-up tickets for a11y pass.
testing_notes: Add e2e steps: enable flag, load dashboard, assert three cards rendered, open first sampled trace, change sampling preset, validate UI telemetry events.
Load test: run console-load-run-2025-11 under staging with 250 concurrent users; gather p95 rendering times and memory profiles.
Reconciliation test: scheduled background job that compares aggregated cost vs. billing sample for top-20 routes over a 7d window; report variance.
Manual QA checklist: help copy present for deferred features, last-known good snapshot display, sampling preset behavior observable in trace output.
notes: This ticket is intended as a surgical MVP cut: preserve high-value observability for on-call and SRE flows while deferring exploratory tooling that would push timeline and infra costs. Keep communication tight with pilot customers and iterate based on telemetry from the feature-flagged rollout.
